effect: For the first hundred days, any criticism of the winner is heard as grief, and any objection as sour grapes.
tell: "Give him a chance" from someone who gave the last one four years of scrutiny and no chance at all.
expires: The first budget, the first appointment, or the first scandal - whichever lands before the hundred days are up.

confused_with.tell: The honeymoan is grace after a win; the crisisglow is authority during a panic. One is granted by the calendar, the other by the alarm.

senses: A temporary condition in which a fresh mandate excuses everything the campaign did not explain, and the losing side is expected to be quiet about it.
It works because a new administration is owed a hearing, and a hearing is easy to extend into a silence. The grace period is real; the only open question is who gets to decide when it ends.
example: *"Every question about the transition was met with **honeymoan** - he just got there, give him time - and the time ran out with the ethics waivers still unsigned."*
